newsitem.title: FRANCE: France sends envoy to Zaire, Rwanda.
newsitem.headline: France sends envoy to Zaire, Rwanda.

text.p: France said on Sunday it was sending cabinet member Xavier Emmanuelli to Rwanda and Zaire to evaluate the situation on the ground ahead of a multinational mission to the region to aid refugees.

The goal of the trip by Emmanuelli, secretary of state for emergency humanitarian action, "is to evaluate the situation in the zone and to show France's solidarity with the humanitarian groups and non-governmental organisations which are working there," an Emmanuelli aide told Reuters.
But French officials were silent on whether Paris was re-evaluating the mission due to the return to Rwanda in recent days of more than 200,000 refugees previously stranded in eastern Zaire.
U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said the United States was consulting allies with an eye to modifying the plan.
But U.N. special envoy Raymond Chretien said a multinational force was still needed in troubled eastern Zaire.
Asked whether the mission might be revised, a French official referred a reporter to a Foreign Ministry statement issued on Saturday.
The statement said Paris was pleased by the refugees' return and added that the aid mission might be completed before the March 31 expiration of its United Nations mandate.
Emmanuelli was expected to arrive in Kigali on Sunday and was to remain in the region until Tuesday, travelling to the Zaire capital Kinshasa before returning to Paris.
The aide denied a radio report that Emmanuelli had been denied permission to land in Kigali.
Rwanda's predominantly Tutsi government accuses France of being partisan after it sent troops to Rwanda in 1994 to help stop Hutu-led genocide of Tutsis and moderate Hutus.

Following Friday's U.N. approval of the multinational peace force, to be led by Canada, France said it was planning the deployment of its forces but gave no indication of when the troops might begin arriving in Zaire.
French defence officials said last week they could have 600 soldiers in place within 24 hours of U.N. approval and another 600 troops within the next 24 hours.
Defence sources said on Saturday, however, that they did not expect French troops to begin heading for Zaire before Monday.
